key_insight: Pseudorandom vane forcing broadens attainable wind-tunnel turbulence, with command amplitude and spectral shape controlling turbulence intensity and integral length scale.
engineering_relevance: Vane inputs can be selected to better match the turbulence intensity and length-scale requirements of a test region.
method: Applied identical angle commands to 15 servo-driven vanes downstream of a 768-fan array operating at constant duty cycle.
Varied vane amplitude and pseudorandom command spectra, with periodic forcing for comparison.
Measured velocity using hot wires at 20 heights and selected spanwise and downstream positions.
evidence_signal: At 60% fan duty, increasing pseudorandom forcing amplitude raised profile-mean turbulence intensity from 6.2% to 23.0%; at 15° RMS amplitude, changing the command spectrum yielded integral scales of 0.88–1.67 m at similar intensities.
watch_item: Inflow properties vary spatially: middle-region minima and downstream changes in integral scale require characterization within the intended test region.
paper_title: Generation and characterization of unsteady inflows in a fan-vane wind tunnel
